content.title: About
content.content: Raw sunflower seed kernels are the edible seeds of the sunflower plant (Helianthus annuus) cultivated worldwide. They have a mild nutty flavor, a crunchy texture, and are commonly used in cooking, baking, and as a healthy snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sunflowers originated in North America but are now grown globally.
Sunflower kernels are one of the richest natural sources of vitamin E, a powerful antioxidant.
The seeds are used to produce vegetable oil, flour, and protein supplements.
Sunflowers are among the fastest‑growing annual crops, reaching up to 3 meters in height within a season.
Raw kernels are often served as a snack, lightly salted or seasoned.

items.title: Rich in vitamin E
items.content: Vitamin E protects cells from oxidative stress and supports skin health.

items.title: Contains healthy fats
items.content: Most of the fat is polyunsaturated, especially linoleic acid, which is beneficial for cardiovascular health.

items.title: Source of magnesium
items.content: Magnesium aids muscle and nerve function and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Provides protein and fiber
items.content: Protein supports muscle growth, while fiber promotes digestive health and satiety.

items.title: Contains phytosterols
items.content: Phytosterols may help lower cholesterol levels in the blood.

items.title: Seed allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to sunflower seeds.

items.title: High in calories
items.content: Raw kernels are calorie‑dense, so they should be consumed in moderation.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: High oxalate levels can contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible people.

items.title: Contamination risk
items.content: Raw seeds can be contaminated with mycotoxins; purchase from reputable sources.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Raw sunflower kernels can be eaten as a snack, added to salads, yogurts, granola, baked goods, or used to make homemade sunflower oil. They can also be lightly toasted or seasoned to enhance flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store kernels in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For longer shelf life, keep them in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent fat oxidation. Discard any seeds with a rancid odor.
